strings.note: Market reading card (the hover panel over an upgrade card): the line under a buff's small green badge and its name, saying this upgrade is the one in the room, so its buff is working. Sentence case, like the rest of the market's reading card; ~30 characters, wraps if longer.

strings.text: Off · wear it to switch it on
strings.note: Market reading card: the line under a buff whose upgrade the player owns but is not using (another piece of the same kind is in the room). 'Wear' is the verb on the card's key (decor.foot.wear) - use the same word. Sentence case; ~34 characters.

strings.text: Works while it is in the room
strings.note: Market reading card: the line under the buff of an upgrade the player can buy tonight - the buff only works while that piece is the one in the room. Sentence case; ~34 characters.

strings.text: Locked · works once it is in the room
strings.note: Market reading card: the line under the buff of an upgrade that is still locked (behind a star or the rung below it). Sentence case; ~40 characters, wraps.
Market reading card: the line under a +0% badge on a piece the bar opened with - the zero the better pieces of that kind climb from. Sentence case; ~24 characters.
Market reading card: the line under the buff of the bar stool, the bar top or a glass line - bought for good, never taken off, so always working. Sentence case; short.

Market reading card: a third, quieter line under two kinds of buff (more customers walking in, a second round) that only work while no other customer is waiting to be served. Sentence case; ~32 characters.
Market reading card: how long the sink runs to wash, after the state line and ' · ' (e.g. 'Working now · 3.0 s'). {seconds} is a number like 3.0. Use your language's short unit for seconds.

Upgrade screen: the caption of a dark band at the top of the shelf, followed by small badges - one per buff the pieces now in the room give (e.g. PRICE +8%, PATIENCE +12%). Capitals; heading face at 16, ~16 characters.

strings.text: NOTHING IN THE ROOM IS WORKING FOR YOU YET
strings.note: Upgrade screen: said in that band instead of the badges when no piece in the room gives any buff yet. Capitals; small face, ~45 characters, one line.

strings.text: ONLY WHAT IS ON SHOW WORKS
strings.note: Upgrade screen: a small note at the right end of that band - only the piece the player has put up in each spot gives its buff, not every piece bought. 'On show' is the words of decor.foot.on_show. Capitals; ~28 characters.
Market reading card for one badge of that band: which pieces in the room make the buff. {pieces} is a comma-separated list of upgrade names. Sentence case.
Market reading card: how fast a shaker tin or a beer tower works, after the state line and ' · ' (e.g. 'Working now · x1.5'). {speed} is a number like 1.5. A plain letter x, as a multiplier.

strings.text: The highest mark bought counts, worn or not
strings.note: Market reading card: the line beside a medal and a comfort number like +0.12 (what this mark adds over the one below it) on an upgrade that has marks (levels) - the room keeps the comfort of the highest mark bought, even when a lower one is the one on show. Sentence case; ~45 characters, wraps.

Market reading card: the line beside a medal and a comfort number like +0.05 on a single piece, a bar stool, a bar-top step or a glass step - the comfort stays for good once bought. Sentence case; short.

A glass line's small buff figure, printed ALONE on its badge beside a heart: {pct} is a number with one decimal, like 0.6. Put the per-cent sign where your language puts it (Turkish +%0.6). Digits, +, -, . and % only: it is set in the arcade figure face.

strings.text: Earned on every drink it goes into
strings.note: Market reading card for a better bottle already behind the bar: the line beside its '+$4 PER DRINK' badge - every drink made with it costs that much more. Sentence case; ~36 characters.

strings.text: The shelf already pours one as good
strings.note: Market reading card for a better bottle: the line beside its (greyed) '+$2 PER DRINK' badge when the bar already has a bottle of the same kind at least this good, so buying it would not raise any price. Sentence case; ~36 characters.
